User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user account in the Giftopia system.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity.

firstName.description: The first name of the user.

lastName.description: The last name of the user.

email.description: The email address of the user.

registrationDate.description: The date and time the user registered.

googleId.description: The Google ID of the user, used for Google authentication. Null if the user didn't sign up with Google.

Product.title: Product
Product.description: Represents a product available for sale in the Giftopia gift shop.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Product entity.

sku.description: Stock Keeping Unit, a unique code for the product.

description.description: A detailed description of the product.

Category.title: Category
Category.description: Represents a category of products in the Giftopia gift shop.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Category entity.

name.description: The name of the category (e.g., 'Birthday Gifts', 'Anniversary Gifts').

showInSubHeader.description: Determines if the category should be displayed in the sub-header navigation.

CartItem.title: CartItem
CartItem.description: Represents an item in the user's shopping cart.

id.description: Unique identifier for the CartItem entity.

quantity.description: The quantity of the product in the cart.

addedDate.description: The date and time the item was added to the cart.

Offer.title: Offer
Offer.description: Represents a special offer or discount.

name.description: The name of the offer (e.g., 'Summer Sale').

value.description: The discount value (percentage or flat amount).

status.description: The current status of the offer.

minimumCartValue.description: The minimum cart value to apply the coupon.

PersonalizationRequest.title: PersonalizationRequest
PersonalizationRequest.description: Represents a user's request for a personalized gift.

userId.description: The ID of the user making the request.

productId.description: The ID of the product to be personalized.

customText.description: The text to be engraved or printed on the product.

customImageUrl.description: URL of the user-uploaded image for personalization.

additionalInstructions.description: Any additional instructions from the user.

createdAt.description: The date and time the request was submitted.

HomepageBanner.title: HomepageBanner
HomepageBanner.description: Represents the main promotional banner on the homepage.

id.description: Unique ID for the banner document (e.g., 'main-offer').

badgeText.description: Text for the badge (e.g., 'UP TO 30% OFF').

title.description: The main headline for the banner.

description.description: The descriptive text for the banner.

buttonLink.description: The URL the button links to.

imageId.description: ID of the image from placeholder-images.json.

isActive.description: Whether the banner is currently active.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to support Giftopia's e-commerce features, including product catalog browsing, shopping cart functionality, and user authentication. Key considerations include authorization independence, clarity of intent, and support for secure list operations. The structure leverages path-based ownership for user-specific data like cart items and incorporates the Google sign-in feature.

Authorization Independence:
User-specific data, such as cart items, are stored under the `/users/{userId}` path. This ensures that access control can be enforced based solely on the authenticated user's ID (`request.auth.uid`) without needing to fetch parent document data. This is a critical design choice to enable atomic operations (transactions/batches) and simplify security rules.

Segregation and QAPs:
Products and Categories are stored in root-level collections (`/products`, `/categories`). This segregation enables efficient and secure listing operations. Security rules can be applied to these collections to control read access.  Since all documents in each collection share the same security requirements, this approach aligns with the Homogeneous Security Posture principle.

Google Sign-in:
The `users` collection stores user data and includes a `googleId` field.  While not directly impacting the Firestore structure, this field allows associating a user document with their Google ID, enabling authentication via Google Sign-In. Firestore security rules can use `request.auth.uid` to verify the authenticated user's ID against the `userId` in the document path for user-specific collections.

Cart Items:
Cart items are stored as a subcollection under each user's document (`/users/{userId}/cart_items`). This reinforces ownership and allows for secure and efficient access to a user's cart data. Security rules can ensure that only the authenticated user can read or modify their own cart items.
